messages.text:
Hello,

I am following up regarding ····.

On September 22, you asked me to confirm whether my shipping address was
still correct, and I confirmed it as requested.

In your email, you also mentioned that your team was reviewing the shipping
and customs details for the replacement unit. However, I have not received
any further update since then.

Could you please provide me with the results of that review, specifically:

   1.

   The exact shipping cost for sending the replacement MGW310 to Brazil; and
   2.

   Confirmation of how HeliumDeploy will handle any customs issues,
   including import taxes, customs clearance problems, return of the package,
   or any other unexpected charges related to the replacement shipment.

As I explained previously, I am willing to proceed with the replacement
solution, since it avoids the extremely expensive international return of
the defective unit. However, I need to understand the total cost and the
customs arrangements before I can authorize the shipment.

This RMA has already been open for many months, so I would appreciate a
concrete update and the proposed shipping arrangement as soon as possible.

Thank you, and I look forward to your response.

Best regards,

Ricardo M.
Handed to the team · Needs the exact shipping cost to Brazil and a written position on customs/import

Hi Ricardo,

Thank you for following up, and I'm sorry this has stayed open so long without the answer we promised you.

You're right to want both numbers before you authorise anything, and I'm not going to guess at either. The exact shipping cost to Aracaju and the written position on customs, import tax, clearance problems and any returned package are being put together now, and a colleague is picking this up today so you get it in one message rather than in pieces.

What is already settled: the defective MGW310 does not come back to us. The replacement ships to the address you confirmed on (address hidden), (address hidden). Nothing moves until you've seen the cost and the customs arrangement and said yes.

The answer comes to you as a reply in this thread.

Best regards,
Sarah H. Support

Hi Sarah,

Thank you for your response and for confirming that I will not need to
return the defective MGW310. I also appreciate your efforts to clarify the
shipping costs and customs arrangements for the replacement.

While we wait for this information, I would like to propose an alternative
solution that might be more practical and beneficial for both parties.

*Instead of receiving another Wingbits MGW310 antenna, would it be possible
to replace it with other cryptocurrency mining equipment available in your
product catalog?*

My proposal would be to receive *one or more mining devices with a combined
value equivalent to the amount I originally paid for the MGW310, as stated
on my original purchase invoice.*

I believe this could be a reasonable alternative to finally resolve this
warranty case, which has remained open for many months.

If this option is possible, I would appreciate clarification on the
following points:

   1.

   Which cryptocurrency mining devices could you offer as part of this
   alternative replacement?
   2.

   Would it be possible to select one or more devices whose combined value
   matches the original amount paid for the MGW310?
   3.

   What would the shipping costs to Brazil be, and how would customs
   clearance, potential import taxes, and any delivery issues be handled?

Please understand that this is simply an alternative proposal. If it is not
feasible, we can continue with the previously discussed replacement of the
MGW310.

My goal is to find a fair and definitive solution for both parties while
avoiding further delays and unexpected expenses.

I look forward to hearing your thoughts on this proposal.

Best regards,

Ricardo M.ça

Hi Ricardo,

Thank you for proposing this, and I'm sorry you had to chase us again. Your frustration is fair.

On the proposal itself: swapping the MGW310 replacement for mining hardware of the same value as your original invoice is a sensible idea, and it is now with Abel and Georges, who decide value substitutions on a warranty case. They have it today, together with the shipping quote and the customs position, so you get one complete answer rather than another partial one.

So you can think it over in the meantime, here is what is live in the catalog right now, in that price range. Harlo B30, 30 TH/s, 899 dollars, currently a pre-order shipping October 30. Magic Miner 40T, 40 TH/s, 799 dollars, Batch 8, pre-order. Bitfortun BS-4, 18 TH/s water cooled, 599.99 dollars. Hammer Miner Thor P2, 10 TH/s, 379 dollars. Hammer Miner DC08 for Dogecoin and Litecoin, 480 MH/s, 539 dollars. Hammer Miner BC04, 6 TH/s, 249 dollars. Combinations are possible, for example the BS-4 with a Thor P2, or a B30 with a BC04, and prices do move, so the figures are confirmed when the swap is set up.

On your third question, I will not guess at it. The shipping cost to Aracaju and exactly who carries import tax, a clearance problem or a returned parcel is the part the team is confirming, and that applies whichever option you take. Nothing ships and nothing is decided without your authorisation.

If you have a preference among those units, tell me and I will put it on the case so the team quotes that exact combination.

Best regards,
Sarah

Hi Sarah,

Thank you for your last response, sent on October 23.

Unfortunately, I must once again express my deep dissatisfaction with the
way this entire warranty process has been handled.

From the beginning, I have cooperated with every request from HeliumDeploy,
proposed alternative solutions, and demonstrated my willingness to find a
reasonable resolution for both parties.

However, *nearly 12 months have passed since this situation began, and I am
still without a definitive solution.*

Throughout this period, several options have been discussed: returning the
defective equipment to the United States, shipping it to a warehouse in
Brazil, replacing the antenna without requiring its return, and, more
recently, exchanging it for other cryptocurrency mining equipment.

At every stage, I patiently waited for the reviews, confirmations, and
decisions promised by your team. Unfortunately, the delays have continued,
and none of these alternatives has resulted in a concrete resolution.

In your October 23 email, you informed me that my proposal to exchange the
MGW310 for other mining equipment had been forwarded to Abel and Georges,
along with the shipping and customs questions, and that I would receive a
complete response.

Once again, I am still waiting.

*What concerns me most is not only the defective equipment itself, but also
HeliumDeploy's excessive and repeated delays in providing an effective
solution to a warranty issue that your company has already acknowledged.*

Throughout this time, I have been left with unusable equipment, unable to
benefit from the product I paid for, while experiencing repeated
frustration from expectations of resolution that have never materialized.

Given this entire situation, I would like to propose a final solution to
bring this matter to a definitive close:

*I formally request that HeliumDeploy consider issuing a full refund of the
total amount I originally paid for the MGW310, as stated on my original
purchase invoice.*

To make this process easier, I am also willing to receive the refund in
cryptocurrency, preferably a stablecoin such as USDT or USDC, if this
payment method is more convenient for your company.

I believe this alternative could significantly simplify the process by
eliminating the need for further international shipments, shipping
expenses, customs procedures, and the risk of additional import taxes or
shipment seizures in Brazil.

After nearly 12 months of waiting, I believe I have demonstrated more than
enough patience and flexibility. At this point, I do not wish to enter
another round of negotiations that could lead to several more months of
delays.

*What I am requesting now is a definitive decision, with a clear answer
regarding the possibility of a full refund and, if approved, a specific
timeframe for processing it.*

I kindly ask that you forward this request directly to the decision-makers,
including Abel and Georges, and provide me with a concrete response within
three business days.

My intention remains to resolve this matter amicably and professionally.
However, I must emphasize that the excessive delays have gone far beyond
any reasonable expectation for resolving a warranty claim.

I sincerely hope HeliumDeploy will acknowledge the inconvenience and
frustration this situation has caused and consider a full refund as the
fairest and most practical way to finally close this case.

I look forward to your prompt response.

Best regards,

Ricardo M.ça

Hi Ricardo,

You are right, and I am not going to defend how this has gone. Twelve months on an acknowledged warranty fault, with you cooperating at every step and answers that kept not arriving, is indefensible. I am sorry.

Your refund request has gone to Abel and Georges directly, with your three business day deadline on it and the full history attached. I want to be straight with you about two things rather than make you another promise I cannot keep. A refund is their decision, not mine, so I will not tell you it is approved before they say so. And on method, our refunds normally go back to the card or account you originally paid with. I cannot confirm a stablecoin payment myself, so I have put your offer in front of them with the rest.

What I can tell you is that this is no longer sitting in a queue waiting for a review. It is with the two people who decide it, flagged as the oldest open case of its kind, and you will have their answer in writing in this thread.

If you still want the hardware route instead, that option stays open until you say otherwise, but I am not going to push it at you after this long.

Best regards,
Sarah
